dossier_meta.statement_text: For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, every graph $G$ and $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$ satisfies one of the following: $G$ contains $k$ pairwise anti-complete $(X,Y)$-paths; or there exists a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ with $|Z|\leqslant k-1$ such that $G-N_{G}[Z]$ has no $(X,Y)$-path.
dossier_meta.context_text: The authors pose this $(X,Y)$-path strengthening of their main theorem (Theorem 3), seeking to reduce the separator size from $78(k-1)$ to the optimal $k-1$. If true, it would have immediate application to the study of induced minors, in particular implying an Induced Grid Minor Theorem for $K_{1,t}$-induced-subgraph-free graphs conjectured by Dallard et al.
